content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/.claude/skills/zimmerMANNReview

Review of a colleague's work. Same architecture as the build chain — ground truth, a gated audit,
then present and stop — tailored to a PR you did not write.

**Intended model: Sonnet 5 at maximum effort.**

**The thing that makes it work:** you hold the ground truth and the adjudication, and delegate only
the reading. Reviewers are cheap and fallible; measurements are expensive and authoritative. Keep
those on opposite sides of the line.

**Input:** `- investigate PR #83, failing: "
Merge info
Changes requested
1 change requested by reviewers with write access.
Some checks were not successful
2 failing, 2 skipped, 5 successful checks
failing checks

* [Deploy Preview / Deploy Preview (push)](https://github.com/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/actions/runs/33848354519/job/100945282184?pr=83)
Failing after 5m
* [QA / Storybook interaction & a11y tests (pull_request)](https://github.com/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/actions/runs/33848358386/job/100945368901?pr=83)
Failing after 3m
Required"` — a PR number.

**Scale to the work.** A two-file PR does not get four reviewers. Nothing too crazy, no
overthinking.

---

## Phase 1 — ground truth. Yours, not an agent's.

### Frame the PR

Base SHA, head SHA, files changed, ±lines. **Use the live head** — a stale ref has already caused a
whole round of re-verification here.

### Requirements — Jira, Confluence, Figma

Build the same requirements picture a PreBuild would build, then judge the PR against it. Every
scope argument, every "this is missing", every "this wasn't asked for" gets decided against these
words — not the PR description's paraphrase of them.

**Jira.** Pull the full ticket: description, ACs, linked work items, and — critically — the full
comment thread. Decisions made in comments routinely contradict the description and never make it
back into the ACs. Flag: untestable ACs · requirements that contradict each other or the comments
· a linked blocker still open · a decision in comments that the implementation may not have seen ·
**evidence that a different PR, branch, or assignee is already working the same ticket.**

**Anything flagged here goes in your next status update to Marcel, even when it's correctly out
of scope for the PR itself.** "Not my concern for this review" and "not worth telling him" are
different judgements — a discovery can be exactly right to leave alone in the diff and still be
something he needs to know exists. Deciding not to act on it is not the same as deciding not to
mention it.

**Confluence.** If the ticket links a PRD, TSD, or integration doc, read it. The Jira ACs are
often a summary; the full requirements live in Confluence. Flag: a Confluence requirement not
reflected in the ACs · a doc that contradicts the ticket · a doc that describes an approach the
PR does not follow.

**Figma.** Read the design systematically — not just the node cited in the PR description.

- **All variants and states:** hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, empty, selected.
  A state the PR doesn't implement is a finding; a state Figma doesn't specify is an open
  question to name, not a reason to skip. **Before concluding a state is simply absent from a
  component, check whether an adjacent or parent element carries that same signal instead** (the
  button not the swatch, the row not the cell) — a concern can be fully handled by the design and
  still look like a gap if you only look at the one element it doesn't live on.
- **Annotations:** interaction notes and spacing/token callouts often hold the real spec detail.
- **Currency:** is the linked node archived or superseded? An archived node that still renders
  is a trap — triage before judging.
- **Tokenisation:** does every colour, spacing, and type value map to an existing `--zimm-*`
  token, or did the author introduce a new one? A new token is Tier 1; confirm it was handled
  correctly.
- **Measurement:** FRAMES and INSTANCES report real boxes (comparable to CSS). TEXT nodes report
  cap-height (not comparable). Never file a mismatch from a TEXT node. Never cross-compare the
  Design System file and the Designs file — they are different sources.

**If the Jira-linked nodes are incomplete, partial, or outdated — stop and ask Marcel for the
correct nodes before continuing.** One node URL per variant and per state, not one per component.
Do not guess at a neighbouring node that looks close, do not proceed on a partial picture, and do
not treat an archived node as the spec. The whole review hangs on having the right design source;
a wrong node produces false findings and misses real ones. This is the one step where asking
beats estimating.

The visual checklist in Phase 2 tells you what to verify in the browser. This step tells you
**what to look for** — you cannot run that checklist without knowing what the design intended.

### The rubric

`.claude/rules/*`, `AGENTS.md`, and the exemplar PR the work should follow. These are what the PR
is judged against — a reviewer applying general best practice instead of house rules generates
noise that reads like signal.

**If the PR edits the rule files it would be judged against, read the rubric at the BASE commit.**
Judging a PR against its own edited rules is circular. Rule-file edits are reviewed separately, as
changes.

### Run the gates yourself — on head and on base

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run test
npm run lint
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
```

Then run them again at the base SHA. **Without a baseline you cannot tell a failure the PR
introduced from one it inherited**, and inherited debt reported as a new violation is the fastest
way to lose a reviewer's trust.

Three false signals, all seen on this repo:

1. **Non-zero at a healthy baseline.** `lint` and `audit:tokens` both exit non-zero on a clean
   tree. Compare counts; ignore exit codes.
2. **A pass having run nothing.** `vitest.config.ts` sets `passWithNoTests: true` — a typo'd path
   filter exits 0 having run zero tests. **Assert on the reported item count, never the exit code.**
3. **A skipped required check looks green.** `detect-changes` can skip `unit-tests` and
   `storybook-test` entirely, and the PR still shows mergeable. Report which checks actually
   *executed* versus which were skipped. A skip proves nothing.

### CodeRabbit is an input, not a verdict

If CodeRabbit has reviewed, read it — then verify it. It has run as low as 1-in-6 correct on this
repo. Its findings enter Phase 2 as claims to test, exactly like anyone else's.

---

## Phase 2 — audit

### Fan out

`zm-tester` dispatches reviewers on **distinct but overlapping** briefs. The overlap is the
mechanism: two agents converging independently is your confidence signal; two disagreeing is where
you learn something.

Give each: the diff, the ticket verbatim, and **your measured gate numbers — then forbid them from
re-running the gates.** Their budget goes on what the gates cannot see.

Angles that have earned their place: correctness and regression · conventions, structure and tier
ownership · contract fidelity, if the PR ports, wraps or overrides something · failure modes and
security · token and styling strategy (bandaid tokens, missing semantic tokens, state
exhaustiveness).

**Design fidelity is yours, not an agent's.** Agents have no browser and no Figma access — ask
them to reason from code and they will, but they cannot see what renders. For any PR that changes
rendered output, run this checklist yourself at the PR's head:

| What to check | How |
|---|---|
| Dimensions and spacing match Figma frames | DevTools computed, vs. Figma inspect |
| Colours resolve to the correct semantic token | DevTools → Computed → colour value |
| Typography uses `textStyle=`, not raw `fontSize` | DevTools → font-size is a `var()` |
| All designed states render correctly (hover, focus, active, disabled) | Tab through + `:hov` in DevTools |
| Responsive behaviour matches the spec | Resize or toggle responsive mode |
| No visual regressions on adjacent components | Scroll the surrounding page |

If a state is not in the PR's recipe at all, no agent will flag it — only you will notice. The
visual checkpoint is the only gate on design fidelity.

**When the PR has a live MRT preview URL, use browser automation — not just your own browser.**
Navigate to the preview URL with Chrome browser tools, screenshot each component across the full
responsive range — not just canonical endpoint widths, but at each design breakpoint and its
boundaries (just above and just below where the layout shifts). Inspect computed styles via
element selectors rather than guessing from code. This produces a concrete, shareable record
(screenshots, exact computed values) rather than impressions, and it runs the same check Marcel
would run himself — so discrepancies surface before comments are drafted, not after.

**Then walk visual and browser-verified findings through one at a time with Marcel before
finalizing them.** Present the screenshot or computed value, let him reproduce or contradict it
from his own browser. This is the step that catches tool artifacts (Popper-positioned layers a
screenshot mechanism misses, click simulations that differ from real interactions, a transition
that hasn't settled when the measurement ran) before they become posted comments. A finding Marcel
has personally verified is a finding you can post with confidence. One that he contradicts is a
finding you drop and learn from — that counts as the verification step working, not failing.

Use **fresh contexts, not forks.** A fork inherits your assumptions about what "done" looks like,
which is exactly what you want tested.

### Scope

`zm-orchestrator` returns the scope verdict — does this PR deliver its ticket, neither under nor
over. Both directions carry equal weight.

### Verify the findings before they reach you

`zm-scorer`, briefed in **findings mode** — it is not scoring the PR, it is scoring the claims:

> For each finding: does it survive scrutiny? Reproduce it or say you could not. Return
> **CONFIRMED** (reproduced from source), **PLAUSIBLE** (consistent with what you read, decisive
> evidence missing — say exactly what would settle it), or **UNSUPPORTED** (the citation does not
> support the claim; say what is actually true). Where a finding's conclusion is broader than its
> search supports, downgrade it — that is the single most common failure mode. Any "X exists
> nowhere" claim must state its search scope in the same sentence.

Expect roughly a third to be wrong. You should not be adjudicating unverified claims.

**This applies to your own findings too, not just an agent's.** Anything you notice directly
while gathering ground truth (a comparison against a related PR, a claim sitting in a code
comment, an assumption about what a value implies) gets the same CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE/UNSUPPORTED
discipline before it is presented as fact — a finding is not exempt from scrutiny just because no
agent produced it. Route it through the same questions: what is the search scope, does one
uncorroborated source actually settle this, and has a stated number been measured or only assumed.

**A claim about how a bug resolves needs the same reproduction as the bug itself.** Verification
effort naturally goes toward proving the failure happens, not toward proving what you claim happens
next — "self-heals on the next hover," "clears on reload," "only affects this one instance." These
read as a supporting detail inside a bigger writeup, not as their own finding, so they skip the
CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE discipline above by default. If you didn't reproduce the recovery, mark it
PLAUSIBLE and say so, exactly like any other unconfirmed claim.

### Classify every survivor

- **In-scope defect** — belongs to this PR. Only these can become comments.
- **Out-of-scope** — real, but not this PR's problem. Name the owning ticket or the person.
- **Nitpick** — cosmetic, brings no value. Recorded, never posted.

A true finding raised on the wrong PR is still noise.

---

## Phase 3 — adjudicate

### Present, in "ELI5 but I'm the FED Lead" register

1. **Gate table** — head versus base, with which checks actually executed
2. **Findings, ranked by what it costs to ignore** — not by severity label, by consequence.
   Each with `file:line`, CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE, and its classification
3. **The scope verdict**
4. **What nobody verified** — the honest section, and what stops a clean result reading as proof
5. **Your adjudications to make**, one at a time via AskUserQuestion

### The verdict is yours

**Approve or request changes is your call, and so is every disputed finding.** The agents produce
findings; you decide what they mean. Where two reviewers disagree, go to source yourself — do not
average them, and do not take the more confident one. Confidence and correctness are not correlated
in agent output.

Name one premise every reviewer agreed on, and make someone attack it.

### Then the comments

Draft general and inline comments for the in-scope defects only. Structure that has worked:

- Verdict up front
- The small cleanups separated from the one thing that genuinely needs the author's call
- A blocker framed as **a question about intent**, citing the project's own doc by section
- The two acceptable resolutions named
- Where an independent tool corroborated, say so

**Natural human language without sacrificing the technical accuracy.** No em-dashes. No Claude or
CodeRabbit attribution. No citation of any local-only doc — cite `AGENTS.md` or `.claude/rules/*`
instead, which the author can actually open. No opening praise or thanks before the substance — a
review comment states findings, it does not warm up first. Watch for jargon-stacking too: a
sentence naming three technical concepts back to back reads like documentation, not like one
person explaining something to another — split it or say it plainer instead.

**Never reveal that a parallel or competing implementation of the same ticket exists**, even in
passing ("the other version of this feature," "the other build") — a review comment is visible to
the whole team, and disclosing a second, independent attempt at the same story is not this
reviewer's call to make. When a content rule like this applies, sweep every drafted comment for
it before presenting the batch, not just the one currently under discussion — a rule caught on
one comment and missed on a near-identical one is a leak, not a style nit.

**Nothing posts until you say so.** Show the full set, post the batch on your go.

---

## The loop

The author pushes changes. Re-review.

**Scoped by default:** which findings the new commits resolved, which they missed, and whether the
fixes introduced anything new. Settled items are not re-litigated.

**Full pass when the diff has genuinely moved** — a substantial new commit, or a change to the
approach rather than the details. **Say which one you ran.**

Repeat until approved. Confirm your own requested changes actually landed rather than taking
"done" on trust.

---

## Ownership and phrasing — every outward-facing surface

Every finding names **who resolves it**: the author, Tim, a designer, a BA, QA.

**Where the owner is senior or lateral, phrase it as a question — never a directive.** "Should this
route via X, or have I misread it?" not "change this to X." Ask confirmatorily.

Before posting, count the asks. A review that mentions one person eight times reads as hiding
behind their authority.

**Be scrupulously fair to the author.** Separate "broke a documented rule" from "hit a gap the
process never covered", and where the process failed them, say so. Flag explicitly any finding
where the fact is true but the characterisation is unfair — better to drop a finding than post an
unfair one.

---

## Hard rules

- **Never write code.** This skill reviews. If a fix is needed on your own branch, that is Build.
- **Never post a comment, a review, or a verdict without an explicit go.**
- **Never resolve a thread you did not open.**
- **Never report inherited debt as a new violation.** Baseline first.
- **Never flag out-of-scope findings onto the PR.** Record them for yourself.
- **Say what you could not verify.** A review that finds nothing has not been shown to be capable
  of finding anything.

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. - vercel:deployment-expert: Specializes in Vercel deployment strategies, CI/CD pipelines, preview URLs, production promotions, rollbacks, environment variables, and domain configuration. Use when troubleshooting deployments, setting up CI/CD, or optimizing the deploy pipeline. (Tools: All tools)

- vercel:performance-optimizer: Specializes in optimizing Vercel application performance — Core Web Vitals, rendering strategies, caching, image optimization, font loading, edge computing, and bundle size. Use when investigating slow pages, improving Lighthouse scores, or optimizing loading performance. (Tools: All tools)

- zm-implementer: Executes one step of a Zimmermann PWA Kit build plan. Use when a planned step needs to be implemented in code. Writes only the files the step names, and stops rather than expanding scope. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-orchestrator: Scope and spec-conformance checker for an in-flight Zimmermann build. Use after an implementation step to judge whether the work delivers exactly what the plan specified — neither less nor more. Reports a verdict; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-planner: Synthesises gathered evidence into an executable build plan for a Zimmermann PWA Kit story. Use after all sources have been gathered, when the findings need to become a sequenced plan with per-step pass criteria. Does not gather evidence itself and does not write code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, WebFetch)

- zm-scorer: Scores an implemented and tested Zimmermann build step and decides PASS or return-to-implementer. Use after the Tester reports. Judges quality against six axes; never edits code. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- zm-tester: Tests an implemented Zimmermann build step across multiple angles and reports findings. Use after the Implementer reports a step done. Finds and reports problems; never fixes them. Dispatches its own sub-agents for parallel angles. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- playwright-skill: Complete browser automation with Playwright. Auto-detects dev servers, writes clean test scripts to /tmp. Test pages, fill forms, take screenshots, check responsive design, validate UX, test login flows, check links, automate any browser task. Use when user wants to test websites, automate browser interactions, validate web functionality, or perform any browser-based testing.
- zimmerMANNBuild: The builder. Executes an approved zimmerMANNPreBuild plan through a closed-loop multi-agent workflow — implement, test, scope-check, score, rework until passed — committing each step and handing off to zimmerMANNPostBuild. Also handles rework from CodeRabbit or reviewer change requests after a PR is open.
- zimmerMANNDevImprover: Looks back over completed build work and improves the build chain. Reads the session transcripts and run artefacts for named stories, diagnoses where the loop failed and whose gap it was, checks whether the skills still cite things that are true, and proposes concrete edits to the build skills and loop agents — applied only on Marcel's explicit go.
- zimmerMANNDevOps: Runs deploys, promotions across environments, tags, release cuts and rollbacks on the Zimmermann PWA Kit. Verifies pipeline state live before every action, shows what each environment is running, and executes only on explicit approval. Reports broken gates and stops rather than working around them.
- zimmerMANNPostBuild: The senior dev pass after a build. Audits what zimmerMANNBuild produced against zimmerMANNPreBuild's plan and findings, runs a whole-feature sweep for uniform defects, writes the PR body, and owns the review conversation — pushing and replying only on Marcel's go.
- zimmerMANNPreBuild: The gate and planner before any Zimmermann PWA Kit build work. Gathers and cross-checks every source — Jira, Confluence, the FED handbook, the codebase and Figma — flags every gap and misalignment, then produces an executable closed-loop build plan and hands off to zimmerMANNBuild. Use at the start of any story, ticket or build task.
- zimmerMANNReview: Reviews someone else's PR as FED Lead. Establishes ground truth, fans out audit angles, verifies every finding before it is raised, then presents for adjudication — Marcel decides the verdict, and comments post only on his go. Loops until the PR is approved.
- zimmerMANNRevImprover: Looks back over completed PR reviews and improves how Marcel reviews. Reads the PR outcome and the review session transcript to judge whether each finding held up, whether anything was missed, and how the review was actually conducted — then proposes concrete edits to zimmerMANNReview, applied only on his explicit go.
- zimmerMANNSprinter: The skill for sprint and agile ceremonies as FED Lead — backlog refinement, sprint planning, standups, retros, and prep for any meeting. Reads Jira and Confluence, drafts what you need to take into the room, and writes to Jira only on your explicit go.
- audit-tier: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.
- code-quality: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
- code-review: AI-powered code review using CodeRabbit. Default code-review skill. Trigger for any explicit review request AND autonomously when the agent thinks a review is needed (code/PR/quality/security).
- contentful-register-component: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
- feature-spec: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
- generate-changelog: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.
- new-component: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
- onboarding: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
- pr-checklist: Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed on the current branch. Pairs with /code-quality.
- project-init: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.
- qa-generate: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.
- scope-check: Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs. Classifies every likely-touched file by tier and verdicts the prompt SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED, rewriting it when needed.
- session-start: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.
- upstream-sync-review: Review the release notes / changelog for a new @salesforce/retail-react-app version before bumping. Lightweight policy — see .docs/upstreamPolicy.md.

- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.

Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. - figma:figma-use: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.

and onClick only on mobile. The test runner runs at desktop width so

Supersedes an earlier note of mine that called this unsettled and said "build flat, don't create
`atoms/`". **That was wrong** — it came from a 19 Aug analysis that was superseded later in the
same session once the decision landed.

**Placement — decided.** Zimmermann design-system components live at:
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/<camelCase>/index.tsx`
(today: `zimmButton`, `zimmIcon`, `zimmLogo`, `zimmNavItem`, `zimmTextInput` as atoms;
`zimmInputAction` as the one molecule; no organisms yet).

**Casing — three families, each correct in its own, don't generalise between them:**

| Family | Casing |
|---|---|
| SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab — must match upstream's import path |
| **ui-kit component** | **`zimmButton/` camelCase — Zimmermann-authored, the default rule** |
| `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase — mirrors upstream exactly |

Kebab-case applies *only* to files mirroring a base Salesforce file. Note also the theme key is
PascalCase (`ZimmTextInput`) while its recipe file is camelCase (`zimmTextInput.ts`).

**Tier — by what the component's own template renders**, not visual size. Atom = renders no other
component; Molecule = only atoms; Organism = ≥1 molecule. An icon passed as a prop doesn't count
(`icon="close"` keeps a Button an atom), and slotted children don't count. When porting from the
F2R library the tier is already recorded as `composes: [...]` — use it rather than re-deriving,
and add `@see f2r/02-design/library/elements/<name>` in the JSDoc.

**Styling surface — decided: a theme recipe, always.** Not inline styles, not a `.zimm-*` class,
not co-located CSS. For a bespoke component wrapping a native element, the `chakra()` factory is
the bridge — native semantics plus recipe styling, read via `useMultiStyleConfig`. **Register the
recipe in `theme/components/index.ts` or destructuring throws at runtime.** F2R `.styles.ts` files
using `.zimm-*` classes are a faithful Figma→CSS transcription and good raw material — *convert
them to a recipe, don't copy the pattern*; never reintroduce `.zimm-btn-*`.

The reasoning against co-located CSS is worth keeping: a stylesheet can only see `var(--zimm-*)`,
which is **derived output at the bottom of the token pipeline**. Author there and you lose
`textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens, responsive arrays, and the
theme drift-guard tests. Not bad CSS — the wrong end of the pipeline.

**Planning fact:** `overrides/app/components/` contains only **seven** directories
(`_app-config`, `button`, `contentful`, `foundation`, `header`, `icons`, `pageContainer`).
`product-tile`, `display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, `footer`, `list-menu`,
`drawer-menu`, `seo` are all still `Origin = Base` despite being referenced throughout
`.claude/rules/`. **Assume most stories pay copy-first**, and expect a rules file's worked example
not to exist yet.

**Why:** getting this wrong adds a fifth competing structure, and my own stale version of it would
have sent a future build in the opposite direction from the agreed one.

**How to apply:** source is Marcel's `~/Dev/fedBuild-manual.md` §2–§3 — **local-only, never
cite it in a PR, commit or code comment** ([[feedback-local-only-docs]]). Cite `conventions.md` /

`overrides/app/theme/index.ts` registers the Zimmermann scale as **`space` only**

deliberately **not** registered. Consequences, both measured during SFCC-55 (session 652997c6):

  **absent** from Chakra's `sizes`, so those declarations are dropped entirely and silently.
- **Typography props** have the same twin: `fontSize: '2xs'` emits 0.625rem where 0.875rem was
  intended, and `'4xs'` emits nothing at all.

**Always use the CSS var on those props** — `width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)'`, never `width: 'xl'`.
Spacing props (`margin`/`padding`/`gap`) are fine with bare keys.

Two related traps from the same work: Chakra resolves a token only as the **entire** value, so
`padding: 'xs 0'` is emitted verbatim and dropped by the browser (use axis props); and a
shorthand declared *after* a longhand resets it (`padding: 0` after `paddingBlock` — use
`paddingInline`).

**Live unfixed instance:** `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:311` has
`fontSize="l"`, which emits nothing. Pre-existing, outside the footer scope, still there as of
2026-08-22.

**Why:** these fail silently — no error, no warning, just wrong or absent CSS. The 576px icon
bug destroyed the entire footer layout before the cause was found.

**How to apply:** `recipeGuards.test.ts` guards the first two cases (bare key on a sizing prop,
bare key in a compound shorthand) and is mutation-verified — run it after touching any recipe.
`theme/index.ts`'s own header comment lists what is and isn't registered.

The tempting high-leverage play in a slim-overrides project: override
`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui/<Name>` so branded styling propagates
into every base SFCC component for free — base cart, checkout and account all inherit
Zimmermann buttons, no import churn, no forked components.

**It does not work.** `shared/ui/index.jsx:29` does `export {Button} from './Button'` — a
**relative** export, which the ccExtensibility resolver does not rewrite. And the consumption
pattern is the wrong way round: **212 base files import the barrel (195 excluding tests); 0 import
`shared/ui/Button`.** (Re-counted 2026-08-25; an earlier note said 208.) So the override intercepts nothing.

This was asserted confidently once and was wrong; Tim's framing (raw components for Contentful)
turned out to be the correct one. An exception note was added to both Desktop docs.

**Why:** it's an architecturally attractive idea that reads as obviously correct, and the
failure is invisible — the override compiles, resolves, and simply never gets imported.

**How to apply:** before scoping a story around "override X and it propagates", grep the base
package for who actually imports the path you're overriding
(`grep -r "from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/<name>'" node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/`).
Distinct from, but same family as, the resolver trap already documented in
`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` — Storybook and Vitest don't load the resolver at all, so a
base-path import silently renders the unstyled base component there.

11	**The discriminator is node type, not a fudge factor.** An earlier version of this memory said
12	simply "Figma reports the glyph box, CSS reports the line box." That's only true of **text nodes**,
13	and the missing half is what makes the rule usable:
14	
15	- **Text nodes** report a **cap-height box** (`text-box-trim: trim-both`, `text-box-edge:
16	  cap_alphabetic`). **Not comparable** to a CSS line box. Measured artifacts: "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs
17	  18, body copy 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18.
18	- **Frames and instances** report a **real box**. **Directly comparable** — so a delta here is a
19	  genuine defect. The `Textfield` *instance* at 44/59 against our 45/68 was a real gap, and the
20	  naive "it's just cap height" rule would have wrongly dismissed it.
21	
22	**Supporting heuristic:** a *uniform* residual across siblings is measurement; a *varying* one is a
23	defect. Three contact items all sitting at +7 after every real cause was removed = the heading's
24	cap box.
25	
26	**Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** In shipped `zimmNavItem.ts`, deriving from `lineHeight` +
27	4.5px padding produced 24/24/24/24/38 = 134 — exactly Figma's `Links` frame.
28	
29	**There are TWO Figma files and comparisons must be like-for-like from one:**
30	`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (design system) and `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (composed page states).
31	Comparing an initial state from the design-system symbol against an error state from the page file
32	produced two wrong conclusions in a row — first "the slot is 59px in both states" (actually
33	`Subscribed=False` 320×44 vs `Subscribed=True` 308×59, with a compensating gap change 40→24: the
34	design **repositions**, it doesn't reserve), then a "reserve the slot" fix that suppressed intended
35	growth when the 68px padded box was already design-correct.
36	
37	**Frames are not breakpoints.** Frames exist at 402/1023/1440; breakpoint tokens are 768/860/1024.
38	The unframed **768–1022 band was genuinely broken** (18px horizontal scroll, 7 wrapped labels) and
39	covers three iPad models in portrait. `flexWrap: nowrap` prevents *breaking*, not *shrinking* — the
40	row refused to break so the words broke instead.
41	
42	**No automated gate in this stack catches a layout defect.** `width: 'xl'` resolving through
43	`theme.sizes` (36rem) blew contact icons to 576px and destroyed the footer on every page while
44	passing tsc, eslint, vitest, local *and* remote CodeRabbit, and Storybook a11y. Only rendering
45	beside Figma found it.
46	
47	**Method notes:** measure `y` relative to the component root (Figma reports frame-relative
48	coordinates); use `domcontentloaded`, never `networkidle`, on a dev server; dismiss the consent
49	banner first; `Range.getClientRects()` gives per-line widths to *prove* a wrap point;
50	`document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable families and is useless — compare widths
51	instead; and **mutation-test layout fixes at mobile**, since two fixes read as Δ0 at 1440 only
52	because a taller sibling column masked them.
53

55	likely artifact, verify uniformity. Frame or instance → treat as real. See
56	[[feedback-prove-dont-assert]] and [[project-chakra-scale-registration]].

**The discriminator is node type, not a fudge factor.** An earlier version of this memory said
simply "Figma reports the glyph box, CSS reports the line box." That's only true of **text nodes**,
and the missing half is what makes the rule usable:

- **Text nodes** report a **cap-height box** (`text-box-trim: trim-both`, `text-box-edge:
  cap_alphabetic`). **Not comparable** to a CSS line box. Measured artifacts: "KEEP IN TOUCH" 8 vs
  18, body copy 26 vs 36, `errorText` 9 vs 18.
- **Frames and instances** report a **real box**. **Directly comparable** — so a delta here is a
  genuine defect. The `Textfield` *instance* at 44/59 against our 45/68 was a real gap, and the
  naive "it's just cap height" rule would have wrongly dismissed it.

**Supporting heuristic:** a *uniform* residual across siblings is measurement; a *varying* one is a
defect. Three contact items all sitting at +7 after every real cause was removed = the heading's
cap box.

**Transfer the rule, not the numbers.** In shipped `zimmNavItem.ts`, deriving from `lineHeight` +
4.5px padding produced 24/24/24/24/38 = 134 — exactly Figma's `Links` frame.

**There are TWO Figma files and comparisons must be like-for-like from one:**
`wPiWmZZOVKnrENUWk2XWWm` (design system) and `QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs` (composed page states).
Comparing an initial state from the design-system symbol against an error state from the page file
produced two wrong conclusions in a row — first "the slot is 59px in both states" (actually
`Subscribed=False` 320×44 vs `Subscribed=True` 308×59, with a compensating gap change 40→24: the
design **repositions**, it doesn't reserve), then a "reserve the slot" fix that suppressed intended
growth when the 68px padded box was already design-correct.

**Frames are not breakpoints.** Frames exist at 402/1023/1440; breakpoint tokens are 768/860/1024.
The unframed **768–1022 band was genuinely broken** (18px horizontal scroll, 7 wrapped labels) and
covers three iPad models in portrait. `flexWrap: nowrap` prevents *breaking*, not *shrinking* — the
row refused to break so the words broke instead.

**No automated gate in this stack catches a layout defect.** `width: 'xl'` resolving through
`theme.sizes` (36rem) blew contact icons to 576px and destroyed the footer on every page while
passing tsc, eslint, vitest, local *and* remote CodeRabbit, and Storybook a11y. Only rendering
beside Figma found it.

**Method notes:** measure `y` relative to the component root (Figma reports frame-relative
coordinates); use `domcontentloaded`, never `networkidle`, on a dev server; dismiss the consent
banner first; `Range.getClientRects()` gives per-line widths to *prove* a wrap point;
`document.fonts.check()` returns `true` for unavailable families and is useless — compare widths
instead; and **mutation-test layout fixes at mobile**, since two fixes read as Δ0 at 1440 only
because a taller sibling column masked them.

**How to apply:** before calling any Figma-vs-code delta an artifact, check the node type. Text →
likely artifact, verify uniformity. Frame or instance → treat as real. See
[[feedback-prove-dont-assert]] and [[project-chakra-scale-registration]].

1	{"additions":2488,"author":{"id":"U_kgDODpvEWg","is_bot":false,"login":"joselitopperezjr-acn","name":""},"baseRefName":"develop","baseRefOid":"a18c68be252375a02dbcee6690d2d5de555ef677","body":"# Description

Implements the wishlist auth gate per SFCC-742 — a `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` organism that
intercepts any wishlist trigger and, when the customer is not logged in, opens a Zimmermann-branded
auth drawer instead. Passwordless email (OTP) and optional Apple/Google social IDPs are supported.
When already registered, the original `onAuthSuccess` callback fires immediately with no drawer
open. All SDK and auth logic lives in `useWishlistAuthDrawer` — the organism is purely
presentational.

Six points worth surfacing before review:

- **Drop-in replacement for `withRegistration`.** `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` wraps a single trigger
  element (any `ReactElement`) and replaces its `onClick` via `React.cloneElement`. Its public API
  is just `onAuthSuccess` + `children` — no SFCC internals leak to the caller.
- **`triggerRef` uses `e.currentTarget`, not `document.activeElement` or `cloneElement` ref
  forwarding.** `cloneElement` ref forwarding requires the child to use `forwardRef` — not
  guaranteed for all consumers. `e.currentTarget` is always the element the handler is attached to,
  reliable across mouse and keyboard. The ref is passed to `ZimmDrawer`'s `finalFocusRef` so focus
  returns to the trigger on close (WCAG 2.4.3 / AC10).
- **`initialFocusRef` wired through `ZimmDrawer` → Chakra's `Drawer`.** `ZimmDrawerBaseProps` gains
  an `initialFocusRef` prop so focus lands on the email input (not the close button) when the
  drawer opens, instead of defaulting to Chakra's FocusLock first-focusable. `ZimmDrawer` was the
  only place this was missing — no base template file needed a copy-first override.
- **`ErrorFallback` sits above `ZimmAuthDrawerContent` in `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer`, not inside it.**
  A boundary inside a component cannot catch that component's own render errors (hooks, early
  function-body code). Moving it one level up means any crash in `ZimmAuthDrawerContent` —
  including a `useMultiStyleConfig` throw on a misconfigured recipe — is contained to the drawer
  content rather than propagating to the app-level boundary and crashing the page. The fallback
  currently returns `null` (blank drawer content), preserving the drawer chrome (title, close
  button) — the Zimmermann-designed error state is a pending requirement, commented in-file as a
  TODO.
- **Social IDP flows (Apple/Google) trigger a full browser redirect.** `onAuthSuccess` is not
  called for those paths — the user lands back already logged in and the wishlist action must be
  re-triggered. This is consistent with SFCC's own `withRegistration` behaviour.
- **Contentful seed script is safe to re-run.** `scripts/contentful/seedLoginDrawerUiCopy.mjs`
  creates 8 `uiCopy` entries for the login drawer microcopy, skipping any key that already exists.
  It paginates correctly (1,000-entry chunks) before building the duplicate-check set. Run with
  `node scripts/contentful/seedLoginDrawerUiCopy.mjs --target dev` after this PR merges.

{"additions":2488,"author":{"id":"U_kgDODpvEWg","is_bot":false,"login":"joselitopperezjr-acn","name":""},"baseRefName":"develop","baseRefOid":"a18c68be252375a02dbcee6690d2d5de555ef677","body":"# Description

Implements the wishlist auth gate per SFCC-742 — a `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` organism that
intercepts any wishlist trigger and, when the customer is not logged in, opens a Zimmermann-branded
auth drawer instead. Passwordless email (OTP) and optional Apple/Google social IDPs are supported.
When already registered, the original `onAuthSuccess` callback fires immediately with no drawer
open. All SDK and auth logic lives in `useWishlistAuthDrawer` — the organism is purely
presentational.

Six points worth surfacing before review:

- **Drop-in replacement for `withRegistration`.** `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` wraps a single trigger
  element (any `ReactElement`) and replaces its `onClick` via `React.cloneElement`. Its public API
  is just `onAuthSuccess` + `children` — no SFCC internals leak to the caller.
- **`triggerRef` uses `e.currentTarget`, not `document.activeElement` or `cloneElement` ref
  forwarding.** `cloneElement` ref forwarding requires the child to use `forwardRef` — not
  guaranteed for all consumers. `e.currentTarget` is always the element the handler is attached to,
  reliable across mouse and keyboard. The ref is passed to `ZimmDrawer`'s `finalFocusRef` so focus
  returns to the trigger on close (WCAG 2.4.3 / AC10).
- **`initialFocusRef` wired through `ZimmDrawer` → Chakra's `Drawer`.** `ZimmDrawerBaseProps` gains
  an `initialFocusRef` prop so focus lands on the email input (not the close button) when the
  drawer opens, instead of defaulting to Chakra's FocusLock first-focusable. `ZimmDrawer` was the
  only place this was missing — no base template file needed a copy-first override.
- **`ErrorFallback` sits above `ZimmAuthDrawerContent` in `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer`, not inside it.**
  A boundary inside a component cannot catch that component's own render errors (hooks, early
  function-body code). Moving it one level up means any crash in `ZimmAuthDrawerContent` —
  including a `useMultiStyleConfig` throw on a misconfigured recipe — is contained to the drawer
  content rather than propagating to the app-level boundary and crashing the page. The fallback
  currently returns `null` (blank drawer content), preserving the drawer chrome (title, close
  button) — the Zimmermann-designed error state is a pending requirement, commented in-file as a
  TODO.
- **Social IDP flows (Apple/Google) trigger a full browser redirect.** `onAuthSuccess` is not
  called for those paths — the user lands back already logged in and the wishlist action must be
  re-triggered. This is consistent with SFCC's own `withRegistration` behaviour.
- **Contentful seed script is safe to re-run.** `scripts/contentful/seedLoginDrawerUiCopy.mjs`
  creates 8 `uiCopy` entries for the login drawer microcopy, skipping any key that already exists.
  It paginates correctly (1,000-entry chunks) before building the duplicate-check set. Run with
  `node scripts/contentful/seedLoginDrawerUiCopy.mjs --target dev` after this PR merges.

# Linked

- Ticket: **SFCC-742** (Wishlist — Login Panel Content)
- Sprint: SFCC — Sprint 7

# Squad ownership

- [x] Squad A (common UI, homepage, navigation, regional storefront, PDP, PLP, cart, checkout, order, payments, returns)
- [ ] Squad B (search & recommendations, promotions, account, store locator, Zimmerse, SEO & analytics)
- [x] Cross-squad — `ui-kits/` atoms and organisms are owned by both squads; both leads notified

# Types of Changes

- [x] **New feature** (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

# Changes

- `components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx` — organism shell; wraps
  trigger, drives `ZimmDrawer` + `ZimmAuthDrawerContent` + `OtpAuth` + SFCC `AuthModal`
- `hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` — all SDK integration (passwordless, IDP, OTP, register modal),
  focus-ref capture, and auth-success side-effect. `DRAWER_ANIMATION_DELAY_MS` constant guards
  the two `setTimeout` calls from drifting independently
- `components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmAuthDrawerContent/index.tsx` — branded login view; composes
  `EmailForm`, `SocialButtons`, `CreateAccount`. Purely presentational — no hooks, no SDK calls
- `components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmAuthDrawerContent/emailForm.tsx` — email input + send-code CTA
- `components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmAuthDrawerContent/socialButtons.tsx` — Apple/Google IDP buttons;
  conditionally rendered per `loginConfig.social`
- `components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmAuthDrawerContent/createAccount.tsx` — "New to Zimmermann?"
  section with create-account CTA
- `components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmAuthDrawerContent/errorFallback.tsx` — React error boundary
  class component; catches all render errors from `ZimmAuthDrawerContent` and its subtree; returns
  `null` (blank) pending Zimmermann error-state design
- `components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmAuthDrawerContent/zimmAuthDrawerContent.css.ts` — co-located
  Chakra recipe; registered in `theme/components/index.ts`

# Sprint Scope

*Draft (2026-06-23). To be refined as sprints are confirmed.*

Defines the dependency order of the build. Claude reads this to understand what code exists at
each stage. **When working in a sprint, do not reference code, components, hooks, or
integrations from a later sprint — they do not exist yet.**

Contentful works/integration will be done as part of each corresponding functional story.

For *what is currently done vs pending* within the active sprint, see
[projectState.md](./projectState.md). This file is the dependency map; `projectState.md`
is the live progress tracker.

---

## Current position

**Sprint 0 — Foundation (in progress).**
See [projectState.md](./projectState.md) for the live breakdown.

---

## Sprint 1 — 29 Jun – 10 Jul

**Squad A (FED):**
- Common UI Components
- Homepage & Navigation (Part 1)
- Regional Storefront (Part 1)

**Squad B (FED):**
*Not started yet* 

---

## Sprint 2 — 13 Jul – 24 Jul

**Depends on:** Sprint 1 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- Homepage & Navigation (Part 2)
- Regional Storefront (Part 2)
- PDP (Part 1)
- PLP (Part 1)

**Squad B (FED):**
*Not started yet*

---

## Sprint 3 — 27 Jul – 7 Aug

**Depends on:** Sprint 2 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- PDP (Part 2)
- PLP (Part 2)
- Cart

**Squad B (FED):**
- Search & Recommendations

---

## Sprint 4 — 10 Aug – 21 Aug

**Depends on:** Sprint 3 complete

**Squad A (FED):**
- Checkout Flow & Delivery (excl. custom payments that will be done in Sprint 6)

**Squad B (FED):**
- Promotions

---

## Sprint 5 — 24 Aug – 4 Sep

**Depends on:** Sprint 4 complete

- Order Management

**Squad B (FED):**
- Store Locator
- Zimmerse

---

## Sprint 6 — 7 Sep – 11 Sep

## Sprint 7

**Squad A (FED):**
- Returns & Refunds

**Squad B (FED):**
- SEO & Analytics (GTM, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Inside Chat, etc)

---

## How Claude uses this file

When implementing a feature, Claude checks which sprint it belongs to and does not reference
components, hooks, or integrations from later sprints.

If a task requires something from a later sprint, Claude stops and asks:
> "This feature depends on [X] which is Sprint [N] work. Should I build a placeholder, or is
> Sprint [N] already complete?"

Reference this file in prompts when sprint context matters:
> "We are currently in Sprint 1. Build the global header skeleton. Do not wire up basket
> state — that is Sprint 3."

271- # Referenced by config/default.js and overrides/app/ssr.js but may not be used by
272- # this project. Marketing Cloud is the PWA Kit default for transactional emails
273-diff --git a/config/default.js b/config/default.js

content.content:
1	name: Deploy Preview
2	
3	# Ephemeral per-branch MRT preview environments. On every push to a feature/fix
4	# branch, creates (or reuses) a dedicated MRT environment, syncs runtime env vars,
5	# builds, and deploys — giving devs/testers a live URL to review during PR without
6	# waiting for a merge to develop. Companion teardown workflow: teardown-preview.yml.
7	#
8	# Every ephemeral target is prefixed `pr-`, so it can never collide with the fixed
9	# named environments (dev, dev1, test, sit, stg, uat, production).
10	
11	on:
12	  push:
13	    branches:
14	      - 'feature/**'
15	      - 'fix/**'
16	      - '!fix/release-*'
17	      # `*` doesn't match `/` in GitHub Actions branch globs, so the pattern
18	      # above alone wouldn't exclude a nested fix/release/<version> naming slip
19	      # — this repo's documented convention is the hyphenated
20	      # fix/release-{version}-* form, but this guards defensively either way.
21	      - '!fix/release/**'
22	
23	# Keyed on the raw branch name (not the derived slug) — concurrency groups are
24	# evaluated before any job/step runs, so the key can't depend on a step output.
25	# cancel-in-progress is deliberately false: a cancelled Actions run does NOT cancel
26	# an already-submitted MRT-side operation (a POST/PATCH, or an in-flight
27	# `pwa-kit-dev push`), so a naively-cancelled run's server-side effects could still
28	# land after its successor starts. Same reasoning deploy-test.yml documents for its
29	# own cancel-in-progress: false.
30	concurrency:
31	  group: mrt-preview-${{ github.ref_name }}
32	  cancel-in-progress: false
33	
34	permissions:
35	  contents: read
36	  pull-requests: write
37	
38	jobs:
39	  deploy-preview:
40	    name: Deploy Preview
41	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
42	    # Deliberately NOT bound to a GitHub Environment. It used to declare
43	    # `environment: dev`, which made GitHub log a real Deployment tagged
44	    # "dev" on every single push to a feature/fix branch -- every PR showed
45	    # a misleading "Deployed to dev" even though the actual target is
46	    # always an isolated pr-<slug> MRT preview, never the shared dev tier
47	    # (confirmed against real Deployment records, 2026-08-25). The binding
48	    # wasn't doing anything functional either: MRT_USER/MRT_API_KEY below
49	    # are already repo-level secrets, the dev-tier Variables this job
50	    # actually needs are fetched explicitly via the GitHub API further down
51	    # (SOURCE_ENV: dev, using GH_ENV_READ_TOKEN) rather than the native
52	    # environment: binding, and `dev` carries no protection rules to lose.
53	    # 12 min target-wait deadline + headroom for npm install/build/push — a
54	    # tighter timeout could cancel the job mid-wait, and a cancelled Actions run
55	    # does not cancel an already-submitted MRT-side operation (see the
56	    # concurrency note above), so the timeout needs real margin over the wait
57	    # budget, not just the wait budget itself.
58	    timeout-minutes: 35
59	    env:
60	      MRT_USER: ${{ secrets.MRT_USER }}
61	      MRT_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MRT_API_KEY }}
62	      MRT_PROJECT: zimmermann
63	    steps:
64	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
65	
66	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
67	        with:
68	          node-version: '24'
69	          cache: 'npm'
70	
71	      - name: Install dependencies
72	        run: npm install --include=dev
73	
74	      - name: Compute MRT preview slug
75	        id: slug
76	        env:
77	          BRANCH_NAME: ${{ github.ref_name }}
78	        run: |
79	          SLUG=$(node scripts/computeMrtPreviewSlug.mjs "$BRANCH_NAME")
80	          echo "slug=$SLUG" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
81	
82	      - name: Read desired proxy config from config/dev.js
83	        id: proxy
84	        run: |
85	          PROXY_JSON=$(node -e "
86	            const cfgs = require('./config/dev.js')?.ssrParameters?.proxyConfigs
87	            if (!Array.isArray(cfgs) || cfgs.length === 0) {
88	              console.error('config/dev.js has no ssrParameters.proxyConfigs')
89	              process.exit(1)
90	            }
91	            console.log(JSON.stringify(cfgs))
92	          ")
93	          echo "json=$PROXY_JSON" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
94	
95	      # Region and proxy config are NOT derived from the bundle push — confirmed
96	      # live this session: two successful `pwa-kit-dev push` calls left
97	      # ssr_proxy_configs null on a freshly created target, and region defaults to
98	      # us-east-2 unless set explicitly. Both must be set here, explicitly, and
99	      # self-healed on every run in case a target was ever created out-of-band
100	      # (e.g. by hand through the MRT console) with the wrong values.
101	      - name: Ensure MRT target exists with correct region/proxy config
102	        id: ensure
103	        env:
104	          SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
105	          PROXY_JSON: ${{ steps.proxy.outputs.json }}
106	        run: |
107	          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
108	          import base64, json, os, sys, time, urllib.request, urllib.error
109	
110	          SLUG, PROJECT = os.environ['SLUG'], os.environ['MRT_PROJECT']
111	          USER, API_KEY = os.environ['MRT_USER'], os.environ['MRT_API_KEY']
112	          DESIRED_PROXY = json.loads(os.environ['PROXY_JSON'])
113	          DESIRED_REGION = 'ap-southeast-2'
114	
115	          token = base64.b64encode(f'{USER}:{API_KEY}'.encode()).decode()
116	          headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {token}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json'}
117	          base = f'https://cloud.mobify.com/api/projects/{PROJECT}/'
118	
119	          def get_target():
120	              req = urllib.request.Request(base + f'target/{SLUG}/', headers=headers)
121	              for attempt in range(3):
122	                  try:
123	                      return json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30).read())
124	                  except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
125	                      if e.code == 404:
126	                          return None
127	                      if attempt < 2 and (e.code == 429 or e.code >= 500):
128	                          print(f'Transient HTTP {e.code} on target lookup — backing off 30s')
129	                          time.sleep(30)
130	                          continue
131	                      raise
132	                  except urllib.error.URLError as e:
133	                      if attempt < 2:
134	                          print(f'Connection error on target lookup ({e.reason}) — backing off 30s')
135	                          time.sleep(30)
136	                          continue
137	                      raise
138	
139	          def proxy_matches(existing_proxy):
140	              if not existing_proxy:
141	                  return False
142	              # Compare the full config per entry, not just path/host — a field
143	              # this repo doesn't use today drifting silently would otherwise
144	              # never trigger the self-heal PATCH below.
145	              norm = lambda cfgs: sorted(json.dumps(c, sort_keys=True) for c in cfgs)
146	              return norm(existing_proxy) == norm(DESIRED_PROXY)
147	
148	          existing = get_target()
149	          if existing is None:
150	              print(f'No existing target for {SLUG} — creating in {DESIRED_REGION}.')
151	              payload = {
152	                  'name': SLUG,
153	                  'ssr_region': DESIRED_REGION,
154	                  'ssr_proxy_configs': DESIRED_PROXY,
155	              }
156	              req = urllib.request.Request(
157	                  base + 'target/', data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), method='POST', headers=headers
158	              )
159	              try:
160	                  resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
161	                  print(f'Create requested: {resp.status}')
162	              except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
163	                  print(f'Create failed {e.code}: {e.read().decode()}', file=sys.stderr)
164	                  sys.exit(1)
165	          else:
166	              print(f'Target {SLUG} already exists (state={existing.get("state")}) — reusing.')
167	              needs_patch = (
168	                  existing.get('ssr_region') != DESIRED_REGION
169	                  or not proxy_matches(existing.get('ssr_proxy_configs'))
170	              )
171	              if needs_patch:
172	                  print(f'Target {SLUG} has drifted region/proxy config — self-healing.')
173	                  payload = {'ssr_region': DESIRED_REGION, 'ssr_proxy_configs': DESIRED_PROXY}
174	                  req = urllib.request.Request(
175	                      base + f'target/{SLUG}/', data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), method='PATCH', headers=headers
176	                  )
177	                  try:
178	                      urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
179	                  except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
180	                      print(f'Region/proxy patch failed {e.code}: {e.read().decode()}', file=sys.stderr)
181	                      sys.exit(1)
182	                  # The PATCH alone updates target config but not the already-running
183	                  # Lambda — confirmed live, the relocation only takes effect after the
184	                  # next `pwa-kit-dev push`, which always runs later in this job.
185	          PYEOF
186	
187	      - name: Wait for target to reach ACTIVE
188	        id: wait
189	        env:
190	          SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
191	        run: |
192	          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
193	          import base64, json, os, sys, time, urllib.request, urllib.error
194	
195	          SLUG, PROJECT = os.environ['SLUG'], os.environ['MRT_PROJECT']
196	          USER, API_KEY = os.environ['MRT_USER'], os.environ['MRT_API_KEY']
197	          token = base64.b64encode(f'{USER}:{API_KEY}'.encode()).decode()
198	          headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {token}'}
199	          url = f'https://cloud.mobify.com/api/projects/{PROJECT}/target/{SLUG}/'
200	
201	          # Fresh create ~5 min, region-relocation redeploy ~2 min, per validated
202	          # session data — poll generously but bounded so a stuck target fails loudly.
203	          deadline, poll_every = time.time() + 12 * 60, 20
204	          while True:
205	              req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers=headers)
206	              try:
207	                  body = json.loads(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30).read())
208	              except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
209	                  if e.code == 429:
210	                      if time.time() > deadline:
211	                          print('Timed out waiting for ACTIVE (persistently rate limited)', file=sys.stderr)
212	                          sys.exit(1)
213	                      try:
214	                          backoff = max(1, min(60, int(e.headers.get('Retry-After', 30))))
215	                      except (TypeError, ValueError):
216	                          backoff = 30
217	                      print(f'Rate limited — backing off {backoff}s')
218	                      time.sleep(backoff)
219	                      continue
220	                  # The create request is asynchronous — a freshly-created target
221	                  # can briefly 404 (not yet visible) or 5xx before settling, not
222	                  # just while waiting on state transitions. Retry those like any
223	                  # other not-yet-ready signal instead of failing the job outright.
224	                  if e.code == 404 or e.code >= 500:
225	                      print(f'Transient HTTP {e.code} — target not visible yet, retrying')
226	                      if time.time() > deadline:
227	                          print(f'Timed out waiting for ACTIVE (last error={e.code})', file=sys.stderr)
228	                          sys.exit(1)
229	                      time.sleep(poll_every)
230	                      continue
231	                  raise
232	              except urllib.error.URLError as e:
233	                  print(f'Connection error ({e.reason}) — retrying')
234	                  if time.time() > deadline:
235	                      print('Timed out waiting for ACTIVE', file=sys.stderr)
236	                      sys.exit(1)
237	                  time.sleep(poll_every)
238	                  continue
239	              state = body.get('state')
240	              print(f'target {SLUG} state={state}')
241	              if state == 'ACTIVE':
242	                  # Read the real hostname from the API rather than assuming a
243	                  # fixed host suffix — that suffix is MRT-account-specific and
244	                  # could change; a hardcoded guess would silently publish a dead
245	                  # URL in the PR comment if it ever did.
246	                  hostname = body.get('ssr_external_hostname')
247	                  if not hostname:
248	                      print('Target is ACTIVE but ssr_external_hostname is empty', file=sys.stderr)
249	                      sys.exit(1)
250	                  with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a') as out:
251	                      out.write(f'hostname={hostname}\n')
252	                  break
253	              if state and state.endswith('_FAILED'):
254	                  print(f'Target entered failed state: {state}', file=sys.stderr)
255	                  sys.exit(1)
256	              if time.time() > deadline:
257	                  print(f'Timed out waiting for ACTIVE (last state={state})', file=sys.stderr)
258	                  sys.exit(1)
259	              time.sleep(poll_every)
260	          PYEOF
261	
262	      # Steps below lift .github/workflows/sync-env-vars-to-mrt.yml's env-var-sync
263	      # logic near-verbatim. The one structural change: source (which GitHub
264	      # Environment to read from) and destination (which MRT target to PATCH) are
265	      # no longer the same value — source is always `dev`+`shared` regardless of
266	      # branch, since there's no per-branch GitHub Environment; destination is the
267	      # computed slug.
268	      - name: Parse syncable keys from .env.sample
269	        id: parse
270	        run: |
271	          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
272	          import re, os, json
273	
274	          # Only keys explicitly tagged `# mrt:true` in .env.sample are synced.
275	          keys = []
276	          pending_mrt = False
277	          with open('.env.sample') as f:
278	              for line in f:
279	                  line = line.rstrip('\n')
280	                  if re.match(r'^#\s*mrt:true', line):
281	                      pending_mrt = True
282	                      continue
283	                  stripped = line.strip()
284	                  if not stripped or stripped.startswith('#'):
285	                      if not stripped:
286	                          pending_mrt = False
287	                      continue
288	                  eq = stripped.find('=')
289	                  if eq == -1:
290	                      pending_mrt = False
291	                      continue
292	                  key = stripped[:eq].strip()
293	                  if pending_mrt:
294	                      keys.append(key)
295	                  pending_mrt = False
296	
297	          print(f'Parsed {len(keys)} MRT-tagged keys from .env.sample')
298	          with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a') as out:
299	              out.write(f'keys={json.dumps(keys)}\n')
300	          PYEOF
301	
302	      - name: Fetch GitHub Environment variables (dev + shared)
303	        id: gh_vars
304	        env:
305	          # Always dev — ephemeral preview branches have no GitHub Environment of
306	          # their own to source from.
307	          SOURCE_ENV: dev
308	          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
309	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GH_ENV_READ_TOKEN }}
310	        run: |
311	          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
312	          import json, os, subprocess, sys
313	
314	          SOURCE_ENV = os.environ['SOURCE_ENV']
315	          REPO = os.environ['REPO']
316	
317	          def fetch_env(env_name):
318	              """Fetch all variables from a GitHub Environment. Returns dict of name→value."""
319	              import urllib.parse
320	              safe_name = urllib.parse.quote(env_name, safe='')
321	              result = subprocess.run(
322	                  ['gh', 'api', f'/repos/{REPO}/environments/{safe_name}/variables',
323	                   '--paginate', '--jq', '.variables[] | {(.name): .value}'],
324	                  capture_output=True, text=True
325	              )
326	              if result.returncode != 0:
327	                  print(f'GitHub API error fetching {env_name}: {result.stderr}', file=sys.stderr)
328	                  sys.exit(1)
329	              out = {}
330	              for line in result.stdout.strip().splitlines():
331	                  if line:
332	                      out.update(json.loads(line))
333	              return out
334	
335	          shared_vars = fetch_env('shared')
336	          target_vars = fetch_env(SOURCE_ENV)
337	          all_vars = dict(shared_vars)
338	          for name, value in target_vars.items():
339	              if value or name not in all_vars:
340	                  all_vars[name] = value
341	
342	          print(f'Found {len(shared_vars)} variables in GitHub Environment: shared')
343	          print(f'Found {len(target_vars)} variables in GitHub Environment: {SOURCE_ENV}')
344	          print(f'Merged total (target overrides shared): {len(all_vars)}')
345	
346	          with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a') as out:
347	              out.write(f'vars={json.dumps(all_vars)}\n')
348	          PYEOF
349	
350	      - name: Sync env vars to the preview target
351	        env:
352	          MRT_TARGET_SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
353	          SYNC_KEYS: ${{ steps.parse.outputs.keys }}
354	          GH_VARS: ${{ steps.gh_vars.outputs.vars }}
355	        run: |
356	          python3 - <<'PYEOF'
357	          import base64, json, os, sys, urllib.request, urllib.error
358	
359	          TARGET  = os.environ['MRT_TARGET_SLUG']
360	          PROJECT = os.environ['MRT_PROJECT']
361	          USER    = os.environ['MRT_USER']
362	          API_KEY = os.environ['MRT_API_KEY']
363	
364	          syncable_keys = json.loads(os.environ['SYNC_KEYS'])
365	          gh_vars       = json.loads(os.environ['GH_VARS'])
366	
367	          payload = {}
368	          skipped_empty = []
369	          skipped_missing = []
370	          for key in syncable_keys:
371	              if key in gh_vars:
372	                  val = gh_vars[key]
373	                  if val:
374	                      payload[key] = {'value': val}
375	                  else:
376	                      skipped_empty.append(key)
377	              else:
378	                  skipped_missing.append(key)
379	
380	          print(f'Keys to sync:    {len(payload)}')
381	          print(f'Skipped (empty): {len(skipped_empty)}')
382	          print(f'Skipped (not in GitHub Environment): {len(skipped_missing)}')
383	
384	          if not payload:
385	              print('Nothing to sync.')
386	              sys.exit(0)
387	
388	          token = base64.b64encode(f'{USER}:{API_KEY}'.encode()).decode()
389	          url   = f'https://cloud.mobify.com/api/projects/{PROJECT}/target/{TARGET}/env-var/'
390	          req   = urllib.request.Request(
391	              url,
392	              data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
393	              method='PATCH',
394	              headers={
395	                  'Authorization': f'Basic {token}',
396	                  'Content-Type': 'application/json',
397	              },
398	          )
399	          try:
400	              resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30)
401	              print(f'\nMRT response: {resp.status} {resp.reason}')
402	              print(f'Synced {len(payload)} env vars to MRT target: {TARGET}')
403	          except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
404	              print(f'MRT API error {e.code}: {e.read().decode()}', file=sys.stderr)
405	              sys.exit(1)
406	          except urllib.error.URLError as e:
407	              print(f'MRT API connection error: {e.reason}', file=sys.stderr)
408	              sys.exit(1)
409	          PYEOF
410	
411	      # Must run after env vars are synced, not before — a target with no env
412	      # vars 500s on every request (confirmed live).
413	      - name: Build and push to preview target
414	        env:
415	          SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
416	        run: |
417	          npm run build
418	          npx pwa-kit-dev push -t "$SLUG" -w
419	
420	      # Deliberately placed after the push above, not right after the "wait
421	      # for ACTIVE" step that first produced steps.wait.outputs.hostname --
422	      # the target existing and being ACTIVE only means the MRT
423	      # infrastructure is ready, not that this PR's own code is live there
424	      # yet. e2e-browserstack (qa.yml) downloads this artifact and points
425	      # BrowserStack at the resulting URL instead of the static test-tier
426	      # RETAIL_APP_HOME, so it actually tests this PR's own changes rather
427	      # than whatever unrelated build happens to be live on test tier
428	      # (test is a deliberate, tag-promoted environment with no guaranteed
429	      # relationship to any given PR -- confirmed with the developer,
430	      # 2026-08-25). Short retention: only needed within this PR's own CI
431	      # cycle, never referenced again after.
432	      - name: Persist preview hostname for e2e-browserstack
433	        env:
434	          PREVIEW_HOSTNAME: ${{ steps.wait.outputs.hostname }}
435	        run: printf '%s\n' "$PREVIEW_HOSTNAME" > preview-hostname.txt
436	
437	      - name: Upload preview hostname artifact
438	        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
439	        with:
440	          name: mrt-preview-hostname
441	          path: preview-hostname.txt
442	          retention-days: 1
443	
444	      - name: Find open PR for this branch
445	        id: pr
446	        env:
447	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
448	          BRANCH: ${{ github.ref_name }}
449	        run: |
450	          NUMBER=$(gh pr list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --head "$BRANCH" --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
451	          echo "number=$NUMBER" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
452	
453	      # Upserts on an exact HTML-comment marker (not a text substring) so a
454	      # coincidental match in someone else's comment can't be mistaken for ours,
455	      # and so redeploys update the same comment instead of spamming the thread —
456	      # the URL is deterministic from the slug and never changes between pushes.
457	      # Pattern mirrors protected-file-guard.yml's Tier 2 warning comment.
458	      - name: Post or update preview URL comment
459	        if: steps.pr.outputs.number != ''
460	        uses: actions/github-script@v7
461	        env:
462	          PR_NUMBER: ${{ steps.pr.outputs.number }}
463	          SLUG: ${{ steps.slug.outputs.slug }}
464	          PREVIEW_HOSTNAME: ${{ steps.wait.outputs.hostname }}
465	        with:
466	          script: |
467	            const prNumber = Number(process.env.PR_NUMBER)
468	            const marker = `<!-- mrt-preview:${process.env.SLUG} -->`
469	            const previewUrl = `https://${process.env.PREVIEW_HOSTNAME}`
470	            const body = `${marker}\n## 🚀 MRT Preview Environment\n\n**Live preview:** ${previewUrl}\n\nTarget: \`${process.env.SLUG}\` · Updated: ${new Date().toISOString()}\n\n_Auto-updated on every push to this branch. Torn down when this PR closes or the branch is deleted._`
471	
472	            // Paginated — listComments only returns the first page (30) by
473	            // default, which would miss the marker on a busy PR and start
474	            // duplicating comments instead of updating in place. c.body is
475	            // optional in the REST payload, so guard against null too.
476	            const comments = await github.paginate(github.rest.issues.listComments, {
477	              owner: context.repo.owner,
478	              repo: context.repo.repo,
479	              issue_number: prNumber,
480	              per_page: 100,
481	            })
482	            const existing = comments.find(
483	              (c) => (c.body ?? '').includes(marker) && c.user?.login === 'github-actions[bot]'
484	            )
485	            if (existing) {
486	              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
487	                owner: context.repo.owner,
488	                repo: context.repo.repo,
489	                comment_id: existing.id,
490	                body,
491	              })
492	            } else {
493	              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
494	                owner: context.repo.owner,
495	                repo: context.repo.repo,
496	                issue_number: prNumber,
497	                body,
498	              })
499	            }
500
