## General review comment (verdict: Request changes)

> Requesting changes. Most of what's below is fixable, but a few things need resolving before this is mergeable as is.
>
> **Tier 1 review is missing.** This touches `config/default.js`, five other `config/*.js` tier files, and a comment-only edit to `overrides/app/theme/foundation/sizes.ts`, all Tier 1 per `frozenFiles.md`. There's no approving review from `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` on this PR yet, so branch protection won't let this merge regardless of anything else here. Worth lining that up early since it's likely the longest pole.
>
> **The PR description doesn't match the diff in several places**, worth reconciling before this goes further:
> - "No Tier 1 file is modified by this PR" and "no production config is touched" are both incorrect — `config/production.js` gets the same passwordless/social login flags as every other tier.
> - The Changes list describes a `zimmFormInput` atom (Figma node 1250:58855) as delivered. It was removed in this PR's own last commit in favor of `ZimmTextInput`'s new `outlined` variant, but the description and the related "Known gaps" note about `--zimm-icon-container-md` never got updated.
> - "Known gaps" says `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` is wired to ProductTile only, with PDP/header out of scope. It's actually the reverse — ProductTile has no changes at all, and the header wishlist icon plus the PDP wishlist button are both wired in.
> - Testing checklist says 705 tests passing and "no new audit:tokens violations, pre-existing 14 unchanged." Running both fresh gives 718 passing and a real 1-to-2 delta on audit:tokens (the new one is at `zimmAuthDrawerContent.css.ts:58`, a legitimate hairline-px exception per `overrideStyling.md`'s Units section, just missing the script's `provisional`/`pending`/`audit-allow:` keyword).
> - Localisation says `translations/en.json` adds the matching keys for the 8 seeded Contentful entries. The seed script's keys are all `login.drawer.*`; the one key actually added to `en.json` isn't one of them.
>
> **Scope question**, genuinely asking rather than asserting: SFCC-742's own description says "Authentication logic and API integration are out of scope for this story and are covered in the relevant auth stories." This PR's core content is exactly that. SFCC-133, SFCC-327 and SFCC-347 look like the stories that line points at, and none of them reference this PR. Was bundling this in deliberate, in which case should those get linked (and maybe re-scoped) here, or would it be cleaner to split the auth/SDK work into its own PR against one of them and keep this one to the panel content itself? Either resolution works, just want the ticket trail to reflect what actually shipped.
>
> **Three real bugs, inline below**, plus a coverage note: none of the three new test files call the actual handler functions with anything that exercises their real branching — they mock at the boundary and assert the mock fired. That's why the bugs below shipped through 718 passing tests clean.
>
> One thing that's not on the author: the ticket's error-state AC is genuinely unanswered — the question was already asked directly in the Jira thread about what copy/UI to use for a failed panel load, with no reply back. Shipping a `null`/TODO placeholder that keeps the drawer dismissible while that's unresolved seems like the right call given no answer came back, not something to hold up this review on.
>
> Smaller stuff, some of it process: a few CodeRabbit findings got fixed in code but never got the in-thread reply this repo's own process calls for — worth a quick sweep. The rest is inline.

## Inline comments

**`overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:144-150`**
> These two effects (this one and the one above it at 130-136) are both keyed only on `[isRegistered]`, so they're not mutually exclusive — if the drawer or OTP modal is open when `isRegistered` flips true and a pending intent flag also happens to be set, `onAuthSuccess` fires twice in the same commit.
>
> There's a second path too: `PENDING_WISHLIST_INTENT_KEY` is set at lines 222 and 243 before the Apple/Google redirect, but it's never cleared in either catch block (230-232, 251-253) or in `handleDrawerClose`. It also carries no product identity. If a social attempt fails or gets abandoned, the flag stays true in sessionStorage. The next time this hook mounts already-registered, anywhere, on any product's PDP, this effect fires `onAuthSuccess` with zero clicks, which per `product-view.tsx:594` adds whatever product that PDP happens to be showing to the wishlist.
>
> Worth keying the flag on the current product ID rather than a bare boolean, and clearing it on the catch/close paths too.

**`overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:193-201`**
> On a non-JSON error response (a 502/503/504 in front of SLAS would do it), `.response?.json()` on line 198 itself rejects, so this returns a rejected promise instead of `{success:false,error}`. Base SFCC's `OtpAuth.handleVerify` (`otp-auth/index.jsx:117`) awaits this inside a `try {...} finally {...}` with no `catch`, so the rejection becomes a genuine unhandled promise rejection there. The shopper sees the OTP input just stop "verifying" with no error text at all.
>
> Might be worth wrapping the `.response?.json()` call in its own try/catch so a non-JSON body still resolves to a generic error message instead of escaping the outer catch.

**`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx:65-76`**
> `ZimmAuthDrawerContentProps` and `EmailFormProps` both have an `isLoading` prop and `EmailForm` does use it (`disabled={isLoading}` at `emailForm.tsx:72`), but it's never passed here, so it falls back to the `= false` default every time. > `ZimmButton` already has `iconLeading`/`iconTrailing` slots (added in this PR) for exactly this kind of icon+label button, but this bypasses it and builds its own container/icon/label recipe instead, per the comment above. Right now `iconLeading`/`iconTrailing` have no real consumer anywhere in the codebase. Given SFCC-588/590/347 are the same shape of control coming up next, is there a reason not to render through `ZimmButton`'s icon slot instead of a second, parallel implementation? > `border.default` is a border-semantic token, used here for `backgroundColor` rather than a border property. > `testing.md` says to clear mocks in `afterEach`, not `beforeEach` — this file has no `afterEach` at all right now. Small one, but it's the one CodeRabbit finding on this PR that seems to have fallen through without a fix or a reply.

content.text:
Two separate causes, one in-scope for this PR and one not.

**Deploy Preview — caused by this PR.** A commit in this PR's own history (`f8a8067a`, "added additional env var to the .env.sample for better MRT preview deployments") added `DEPLOY_TARGET=` tagged `# mrt:true` to `.env.sample`. The `deploy-preview.yml` workflow parses every `# mrt:true`-tagged key out of `.env.sample` and syncs it to the MRT preview target's env vars. MRT rejects the whole batch with `400: {"name":["Use an environment variable name that isn't reserved."]}` because `DEPLOY_TARGET` is a name their platform reserves for itself. I bisected the run history: every push before that commit passed, every push since has failed with this exact error.

It looks like a leftover from an abandoned approach — the very next commit fixed the actual underlying problem a different way (`config/default.js`'s `IS_PREVIEW_TARGET`, so ephemeral `pr-*` preview targets stop falling through to a hardcoded `false`), which made the `.env.sample` entry unnecessary. Nobody removed it, so it's still there breaking every push on this branch. Fix is a two-line deletion in `.env.sample`.

**Storybook interaction & a11y tests — not caused by this PR.** `http-server` and `wait-on` (used to serve the built Storybook and wait for it to come up before running `test-storybook`) aren't pinned as devDependencies, so every CI run does a cold `npx` registry install of them, racing a fixed 60-second `wait-on` timeout. On this run the actual Storybook build succeeded ("Storybook build completed successfully" in the log); the server just never came up in time afterward. I checked this isn't specific to this PR — it failed today on two completely unrelated PRs too (`feature/SFCC-662-adyen-pwa-install`, `feature/sfcc-731-pdp-gallery`), intermixed with passes on those same branches at other times. It's a pre-existing, repo-wide flake in `qa.yml`, owned by Integration/SI Partner per `frozenFiles.md`, not something the PR author can fix.

---
name: audit-tier
description: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.
---

Identify the protection tier and owner of a file or directory in this codebase.

The path to audit is: $ARGUMENTS

## What to output

**1. Tier**
- Tier 1 (Frozen) — must not be modified without explicit owner approval
- Tier 2 (Protected) — feature branch only, requires second-developer PR review
- Tier 3 (Squad-owned) — only the owning squad should be prompting Claude here
- Tier 4 (Feature-local) — freely editable on a feature branch

Check against:
- [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md) for Tier 1
- [.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md](../../rules/protectedFiles.md) for Tier 2
- `.claude/rules/squadA.md` and `.claude/rules/squadB.md` for Tier 3 *(if absent, infer from path: checkout/cart/payments = Squad A; PDP/PLP/search/account = Squad B)*

**2. Owner**
Design System / Integration / SI Partner / Squad A / Squad B / Both Squads

**3. Can Claude Code modify it?**
- Tier 1: No. Developer must name the file explicitly in the prompt AND confirm owner approval.
- Tier 2: Yes on a feature branch — second-developer PR review required before merging.
- Tier 3: Yes — but only the owning squad should be running Claude in this area.
- Tier 4: Yes, freely.

**4. Import blast radius**
Run this to check how many non-test, non-story files import it (from `overrides/app/` — the customisation surface):
```bash
grep -rl "$(basename "$ARGUMENTS" | sed 's/\.[tj]sx\?$//')" overrides/app --include="*.ts" --include="*.tsx" \
  | grep -v '\.test\.' | grep -v '\.stories\.' | wc -l
```
If more than 5, flag it as **high blast radius** — a change here breaks many consumers.

**5. Next step**
Specific action for the developer — e.g.:
- "Message #design-system before asking Claude to touch this"
- "This is Tier 3 Squad A — if you're Squad B, message the Squad A Lead first"
- "This is Tier 4 — safe to include in your prompt with an explicit file path"

---
name: fix-deploy-preview-env
description: Fix the "Deploy Preview" GitHub Action failing with "Use an environment variable name that isn't reserved." Use on feature/SFCC-742_wishlist-loginpanel-content (or any branch carrying its .env.sample change) when that check fails.
---

Diagnosed root cause (SFCC-742, PR #83, reviewed 2026-09-04): a `.env.sample` entry tagged
`# mrt:true` gets auto-synced by [.github/workflows/deploy-preview.yml](../../../.github/workflows/deploy-preview.yml)'s
"Parse syncable keys from .env.sample" step to the ephemeral MRT preview target's environment
variables. MRT rejects the sync with `400: {"name":["Use an environment variable name that isn't
reserved."]}` because one of those keys, `DEPLOY_TARGET`, collides with a name the platform
reserves for itself. Confirmed by bisecting this branch's own Action run history: every push
before the commit that added this entry passed, every push since has failed identically — it is
not intermittent and will not fix itself on retry.

This skill only fixes **this** failure. If "Storybook interaction & a11y tests" is also failing,
that is a separate, pre-existing, repo-wide CI flake unrelated to this branch (missing pinned
`http-server`/`wait-on` devDependencies racing a fixed timeout) — owned by Integration/SI Partner
per [frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md), not something to fix here. Re-running that check
is the right move there, not editing anything.

## What to do

1. Confirm the current branch is not `develop` or `main` (`git branch --show-current`) — stop if it is.
2. Open `.env.sample` and find this exact block, immediately after the `EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID` entry:
   ```
   # scope:tier
   # mrt:true
   DEPLOY_TARGET=
   ```
   If it isn't there, this branch doesn't have the problem this skill fixes — stop and say so
   rather than editing anything else.
3. Delete those three lines, and the blank line separating them from the next entry (so no double
   blank line is left behind). Nothing else in the file should change.
4. Run `git diff .env.sample` and confirm the diff shows only that removal — three content lines
   plus at most one blank line, nothing else touched.
5. Explain briefly why this is safe to remove outright, not a workaround: `config/default.js`'s
   `IS_PREVIEW_TARGET` check (added in the very next commit on this branch) already solves the
   real problem this entry was reaching for — an ephemeral `pr-*` preview target has no
   `config/<tier>.js` of its own, so it was falling through to `config/default.js` with
   `passwordless`/`social` login hardcoded `false`. The `.env.sample` entry was an earlier,
   abandoned attempt at the same fix, and confirm it via
   `grep -rn "DEPLOY_TARGET" overrides/ config/` — the only remaining reference should be inside
   that `IS_PREVIEW_TARGET` line, never sourced from `.env.sample`/`process.env` anywhere else.
6. Show the resulting diff and stop there. Do not commit, push, or open/update a PR — per this
   repo's own [Hard Rule #15](../../../AGENTS.md#hard-rules), that only happens on the developer's
   explicit ask, separate from running this skill.
